transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brought you in to see me?

I guess... people say my talking gets all mixed up. I try to explain things to them, like... about the keys, and then the jail... the prayer rug... chess pieces. I don't know. They just tell me they can't follow what I'm saying. That's why I'm here.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed your mood feeling unusually high, elated, or full of energy, more than what's normal for you?

I don't know about elated. I guess... sometimes I just feel real high up. Like... powerful. I end up laughing, talking real loud to folks. 

But... if they start questioning me about things, I... I can snap. Just yell at 'em over some little thing. I don't know.
How many days in a row have you been feeling this 'high' and powerful, with lots of energy and irritability?

I don't really count the days. If you... if you add it all up, I guess... all those times with the high energy, not sleeping much, having all these big plans... it's been about a year and eight months altogether. Something like that.
Does this confused, mixed-up talking happen only during those high-energy, irritable periods, or does it also occur when your mood feels normal and even, in between those episodes?

I guess... it happens other times, too. There's been calmer weeks. Times when I ain't especially high, and I'm not deeply depressed either. Just... even. 

But... I don't know. Even then, for more than two weeks during those calm times... I still heard the man in the vents. And I could tell people in the building were signaling about me. So... yeah. I guess my talking gets mixed up then, too.

Thinking about the whole time you've been having these experiences, would you say the voices and feeling that people are signaling about you have been present most of the time—even during the calm, stable periods—or do they mainly show up only during your high-energy or low mood episodes?

I don't know about most of the time. I just... I know it's there when I'm up, too. Like when I was only getting a few hours of sleep... making all those big plans for the buildings... I still heard the voice in the vent. And the hallway lights... I was sure they were sending warnings about me then, too. So... yeah.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient describes a manic/mixed mood episode (elevated, expansive/irritable mood, decreased need for sleep, grandiosity, pressured/loud speech, over ~20 months cumulative) occurring concurrently with disorganized speech, auditory hallucinations ('man in the vents'), and persecutory delusions (being 'signaled about'). Critically, these psychotic symptoms (hallucinations and delusions) persisted for more than 2 weeks during clearly defined euthymic periods when mood symptoms were absent, ruling out a primary mood disorder with psychotic features (F31). The mood episode has also been present for a substantial portion of the total illness duration, and psychotic symptoms occur both during and outside mood episodes, meeting criteria for schizoaffective disorder rather than schizophrenia (which would require mood episodes to be brief relative to psychotic illness) or bipolar disorder with psychotic features (which requires psychotic symptoms only during mood episodes).
